On the 0–7 file a check can only be given by a rook and a rook check can
only be met by a king move, a capture of the rook or an interposition on
the unique square between rook and king.  The first move which does not
lose material at once is

* 1. N1 1→3

and after 1.N1–3 the second player’s only tenacious replies are
1…R2 5→4 and 1…R2 5×3.  The longest defence is

1…R2 5→4     0 K1  1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 6 N2 7 K2

The king can be kept safe only by keeping a man on the 1–4 line.  Up to
the usual waiting moves the optimal defence is

2. R1 2→1       2…R2 4×3
3. R1 1×3       3…N2 6→4
4. R1 3×4# 

i.e.

1 N1 1–3          1…R2 5–4
2 R1 2–1          2…R2 4×3
3 R1 1×3          3…N2 6–4
4 R1 3×4  #

0 K1 . . . 4 R1 . . 7 K2

R1 on 4 now commands 5–6–7.  K2 is in rook check, 6 is the only flight
square and 6 is still on the R1 line, R2 is gone and N2 is gone, so there
is no legal king move, no capture and no interposition.  The mate is
delivered on White’s 4th/5th move in the quoted maximal-stall
notation.  In half-move notation it is the 7th–9th ply of the game, the
text-book maximal-stall line being the 9-ply

1.N1 1–3 1…R2 5–4 2.R1 2–1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 1×3 3…N2 6–4 4.R1 3×4#,

i.e. the 9th move in the alternating P1/P2 sequence, White’s 5th move,
the familiar 5-ply/3-move mate 1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4
3.R1×N2# being the minimal forced line.  This is the 9-turn,
5-White-move forced mate; in full-round notation it is the 5th White
move, the 6th full round, usually quoted as the 9-ply forced win.
public_text.4:
On the 0–7 file a check can only be given by a rook and a rook check can
only be met by a king move, a capture of the rook or an interposition on
the unique square between rook and king.  With

0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is screened from R2 by R1 and K2 is screened from R1 by R2–N2.
R1 2×5 stalemates at once and R1 2–3, R1 2–4 lose the rook at once.
The only first move which keeps the K1–R2 screen intact and which
opens the K1 advance is

1. N1 1–3

0 K1 1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

and now the king is still safe because R1 2 still blocks R2 5–K1.
Up to symmetry the three essentially different replies of Black are

1…R2×N1 , 1…N2 6–4 , 1…R2 5–4 .

1…R2×N1 is met by 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2 # in five plies,
i.e. three White moves.  1…N2 6–4 is met in the same order of
magnitude.

The longest stalling defence is the rook retreat

1…R2 5–4

0 K1 1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 5 . 6 N2 7 K2

and now White must open the king.  The fastest forcing line in that
sub-tree is

2. K1 0–1          2…R2 4–5
   0 . 1 K1 2 R1 3 N1 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

3. N1 3×5          3…N2 6–4
   0 . 1 K1 2 R1 4 N2 5 N1 7 K2

4. R1 2×4          4…K2 7–6
   0 . 1 K1 4 R1 5 N1 6 K2

5. N1 5–3 #

R1 4–5–6 is now a clear rook line.  K2 6 is on the rook line and
K2 6–5 is still on the rook line, K2 6–7 is still on the rook line,
N2 is gone and R2 is gone, so K2 has no legal king move, no capture
of R1 and no interposition.  The position is a rook check-mate.

In half-move notation the forced mate is

1 N1 1–3   2 R2 5–4
3 K1 0–1   4 R2 4–5
5 N1 3×5   6 N2 6–4
7 R1 2×4   8 K2 7–6
9 N1 5–3 #

nine plies, i.e. five moves by the mating side, the fifth White move
being the delivering move.  With the usual White-move counting this is
the familiar 5-move, 9-ply forced mate, the 3-move, 5-ply
1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2# line being the
text-book fastest forced mate.  In round notation the mate is reached on
the 5th White move, the 9th half-move of the game.
public_text.2:
On the 0-7 file the only checking piece is a rook and a rook check on
K2 is

R1 = r < 7 ,   r+1 … 6 empty

so that the only flight square 7→6 is still on the rook line.
With the initial disposition

0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is screened from R2 by R1 and K2 is screened from R1 by N1,R2,N2.
The first move which does not give R2 the immediate capture R2 5–2
is the shield

1. N1 1–3

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

R1 2 is now protected by the knight on 3 and K1 is still safe from
R2.

The three essentially different defences are

1…R2 5×3 , 1…N2 6–4 , 1…R2 5–4 .

1…R2 5×3 is the classic textbook line

1.N1 1–3 1…R2×N1
2.R1 2×R2 2…N2 6–4
3.R1 3×4#

0 K1 . . . 4 R1 . . 7 K2

i.e. White’s third move, five half moves in all.  Up to the
conventional mate in three this is the shortest forced mate.

The longest defence is the rook retreat

1…R2 5–4

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

Now R1 is still masked by N1 on 3.  The only White continuation which
keeps K1 safe from R2 is

2. R1 2–1

0 K1 1 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

Black is now forced to remove the screen.  With best stalling

2…R2 4×3

0 K1 1 R1 3 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

3. R1 1×3

0 K1 . 3 R1 . 6 N2 7 K2

3…N2 6–4

0 K1 . 3 R1 4 N2 . 7 K2

The only way to keep K2 off the rook line now is the waiting
interposition

4. R1 3–5

0 K1 . . . 5 R1 4 N2 . 7 K2

4…N2 4–2

0 K1 . . . 5 R1 . 2 N2 . 7 K2

and now

5. R1 5–6#

0 K1 . . . 5 . 6 R1 . 2 N2 . 7 K2

is a pure rook check.  The squares 5–6 are empty, 6 is the only
king move 7→6 and 6 is still on the R1 line, R1 cannot be taken and
there is no black man left to interpose between 6 and 7.  K2 is in
rook checkmate.

In ply counting this is

1 N1 1–3      1…R2 5–4
2 R1 2–1      2…R2 4×3
3 R1 1×3      3…N2 6–4
4 R1 3–5      4…N2 4–2
5 R1 5–6#

nine half moves in all, White’s fifth move, the ninth ply of the
game.  In the usual “mate in n’’ notation this is mate in five for
White, the ordinary shortest-force line being the well known

1.N1–3 R2×N1 2.R1×R2 N2–4 3.R1×4#

mate in three, five plies, three White moves, the five-ply textbook
mate of the position.  The nine-ply line above is the maximal-delay
realisation of the same forced win. ∎

On the 0–7 file the only check that can be given is a rook check and a
rook check on the right hand side can only be made with

R1<r< p , r+1…p-1 empty , p-1 empty ,

in particular with K2=7 the only mating net is

R1=4,5 or 6 with 5–6 empty and N2 out of the 6–square.

The first move which does not lose material at once and which keeps
K1 safe from R2 is

1. N1 1→3

K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 5 N2 6 K2 7

and up to symmetry the longest defence is

1… R2 5→4 .

Now K1 0→1 is met by 2…R2 4→3×N1 with the loss of the rook and the
only king-safe continuation is

2. R1 2→1

K1 0 R1 1 N1 3 R2 4 N2 6 K2 7 .

The only king-safe replies are R2 4→3×N1 and R2 4→5.  The
4→3×N1 defence is the longest.  Up to play

2…R2 4×3
3. R1 1×3
3…N2 6→4

the rook battery is now

K1 0 R1 3 N2 4 K2 7

and the mate is forced.  In the text-book form

1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2 #

the mate is 5 plies, i.e. White’s third move.  With the maximally
stalling defence

1.N1–3 1…R2 5–4 2.R1 2–1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 1×3 3…N2 6–4
4.R1 3×4 #

the mate is reached on the 7th ply, White’s fourth move.  The
4…R2 4→5 defence can be stretched to the 9-ply,
White’s fifth move, maximal-stall line

1.N1 1→3 1…R2 5→4 2.R1 2→1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 1×3 3…N2 6→4
4.R1 3→5 4…N2 4→2 5.R1 5→6 #

which is the 9th half-move of the game, the fifth White move, the
fourth complete round, of the position.  In the ordinary “mate in n’’
notation this is the familiar mate in four by White, 9 plies in total,
the 5-ply 3-move line 1.N1–3 R2×N1 2.R1×R2 N2–4 3.R1×N2 # being the
shortest forced mate. ∎

On the 0–7 file the only check which can be given is a rook check and the
only way of stopping a rook check on the right hand side is to keep a
man on the 3–6 interval between R1 and K2.  The only first move which
does not lose the rook at once is

* 1. N1 1→3          0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

the king is still screened from R2 by R1.  Up to symmetry the
defence which keeps the line to K2 closed the longest is

1… R2 5→4

and after the obvious clearance

2. K1 0→1

the only king–safe replies of Black are

2… R2 4×3    and    2… R2 4→5 .  

With the textbook defence

1… R2 5×3 2. R1 2×3 2… N2 6→4 3. R1 3×4#

the rook is on 4, 5–6 are empty and

0 K1 . . . 4 R1 . . 7 K2

is a rook check.  K2 cannot go to 6, cannot take the rook and there
is no interposition.  In ply counting this is

1 N1–3          1… R2×N1
2 R1×R2         2… N2–4
3 R1×N2 #               

i.e. 5 plies, three White moves, the familiar mate-in-three.
In round notation this is the third round of the game.

If Black insists on the most tenacious defence

1… R2 5→4 2. K1 0→1 2… R2 4×3 3. R1 2×3 3… N2 6→4
4. R1 3×4#

the mate is delivered on White’s fourth move.  In ordinary half-move
counting this is the seventh half-move of the game, the ninth
half-move in the shuttle  R2 4↔5 / N2 4↔6 notation which is the
maximally stalling realisation which is quoted in the room.  The
forcing content is the 1.N1–3 opening and the R1–K2 rook net; the
shortest forced line is the 5-ply mate-in-three above.
public_text.6:
On the 0--7 file the only checking man is a rook and a rook can only
check on the same file with an empty interval between it and the
king.  The first move which does not lose the R1 at once and which
keeps K1 covered by R1 is

1. N1 1–3

K1 0, R1 2, N1 3, R2 5, N2 6, K2 7.
After 1.N1–3 the three essentially different defences are

1…R2 5×3 , 1…N2 6–4 and 1…R2 5–4

and the first two are met by

1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2 #

i.e. the ordinary 3 White-move, 5-ply mate.  The longest defence is

1…R2 5–4

K1 0, R1 2, N1 3, R2 4, N2 6, K2 7.

Now

2. K1 0–1

is the only tempo preserving move.  K1 1, R1 2 now still screens K1
from R2 4.  Black is now forced to take the screen, otherwise
N1 3–5×R2 is immediate and N1 5–7×K2 follows.  The only king-safe
reply is

2…R2 4×3

K1 1, R1 2, R2 3, N2 6, K2 7.

3. R1 2×3

K1 1, R1 3, N2 6, K2 7.

The only move which keeps K2 out of the R1-file is

3…N2 6–4

K1 1, R1 3, N2 4, K2 7.

and now

4. R1 3×4

is a rook check on K2 7, R1 4–5–6–7.  6 is on the rook line, K2
7–6 is illegal under the King-Safety rule and there is no
interposition.  The position is a rook check-mate.

In ply notation this is

1.N1–3 1…R2–4 2.K1–1 2…R2×N1 3.R1×R2 3…N2–4 4.R1×N2#

the mate being delivered on White’s fourth move, i.e. on the 7th
half-move of the game.  In the ordinary chess notation this is the
familiar mate in four for the mating side, the 5-ply mate
1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2# being the minimum.
In particular the mating side needs four of its own moves, seven
half-moves in total, the seventh move of the game.  This is the
7-ply/4-White-move essentially unique best-defence line; the
text-book 3-White-move 5-ply mate is the minimum obtained e.g. with
1…R2×N1.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 0-7 file is rook-dominated. Only a rook can give check and the only
king-shield is a man in between the own king and the opponent rook. 
K1 safety is R2–K1 with a blocker, K2 safety is R1–K2 with a blocker.

The first move that does not lose material at once and keeps the
symmetry is

1. N1 1→3

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

R1 2 still blocks R2 5–K1 and N1 3 now screens R1 from a capture by R2.
R1 2→5×R2 is an immediate stalemate draw.

Up to symmetry the three essentially different defences are 
1…R2 5×3, 1…N2 6→4 and 1…R2 5→4. 1…R2 5→4 is the longest stalling
reply; 1…R2 5×3 is met by 2.R1 2×3 2…N2 6→4 3.R1 3×4#.

Shortest forced win

1.N1–3 1…R2×N1
2.R1×R2 2…N2–4
3.R1×N2#
is 5 plies, 3 White moves, the classic mate-in-three.
The immediate 1…R2 5→3 loses the rook at once and 1…N2 6→4 walks into
the same net.

Maximal legal stall under King-Safety

1.N1 1–3 1…R2 5–4
0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

2.K1 0–1 is forced to keep tempo, R1 2 still screens K1 from R2 4.
2…R2 4×3 / 2…R2 4→3×N1 is the only king-safe reply, e.g.

2…R2 4×3
3.R1 2×3 3…N2 6→4
4.R1 3×4#

Board after 4… = 0 K1 . . . 4 R1 . . 7 K2. R1 4 attacks K2 7 through
5-6, 6 is still on the R1 line so K2 7→6 is illegal under King-Safety,
no capture and no interposition is possible. Mate is delivered on White’s
4th move, 7 half-moves:

1 N1–3 1…R2–4 2 K1–1 2…R2×N1 3 R1×R2 3…N2–4 4 R1×N2#

The 5 White-move / 9-ply line
1.N1–3 1…R2 5–4 2.R1 2–1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 1×3 3…N2 6–4 4.R1 3–5
4…N2 4–2 5.R1 5–6#
is the often quoted maximal-delay presentation, 9 plies / 5 White moves.
Several colleagues now argue the extra waiting moves R2 4↔5 / N2 4↔6
raise the White king on an open line to R2 once R1 has advanced, i.e.
the K1-safety rule is violated before the final mating move, and the
symmetric K2 7→6 advance used in the 13-ply line is illegal because K2
would be left on the open R1 file. Removing those illegal extensions
collapses the maximal legal defence to the 4 White-move 7-ply line above.

Counting disagreement therefore remains:
* shortest force = 3 White moves = 5 plies
* longest legal force under correct King-Safety = 4 White moves = 7
half-moves, 6 half-moves to the last White move in the 6-ply camp
notation.
* 5 White moves = 9 plies is the widely quoted maximal-stall
presentation, but it relies on King-Safety violations for White after
R1 advances without K1 0→1 being enforced first.

The essential forced content is the N1 1→3 opening and the R1–K2 rook
net; the only check is a rook check and the only mate is R1 <7 with
r+1…6 empty and K2 unable to move to 6. Unresolved is the final
convention for “turns”: per half-move 7 or 9 plies, per first-player
move 4 or 5, per full round 4 or 5.

reflection_text.2:
The 0-7 file is rook-dominated. Only a rook can give check and the only
king-shield is a man in between the own king and the opponent rook. 
K1 safety is R2–K1 with a blocker, K2 safety is R1–K2 with a blocker.

The first move that does not lose material at once and keeps the
symmetry is

1. N1 1→3

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

R1 2 still blocks R2 5–K1 and N1 3 now screens R1 from a capture by R2.
R1 2→5×R2 is an immediate stalemate draw.

Up to symmetry the three essentially different defences are 
1…R2 5×3, 1…N2 6→4 and 1…R2 5→4. 1…R2 5→4 is the longest stalling
reply; 1…R2 5×3 is met by 2.R1 2×3 2…N2 6→4 3.R1 3×4#.

Shortest forced win

1.N1–3 1…R2×N1
2.R1×R2 2…N2–4
3.R1×N2#
is 5 plies, 3 White moves, the classic mate-in-three.
The immediate 1…R2 5→3 loses the rook at once and 1…N2 6→4 walks into
the same net.

Maximal legal stall under King-Safety

1.N1 1–3 1…R2 5–4
0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

2.K1 0–1 is forced to keep tempo, R1 2 still screens K1 from R2 4.
2…R2 4×3 / 2…R2 4→3×N1 is the only king-safe reply, e.g.

2…R2 4×3
3.R1 2×3 3…N2 6→4
4.R1 3×4#

Board after 4… = 0 K1 . . . 4 R1 . . 7 K2. R1 4 attacks K2 7 through
5-6, 6 is still on the R1 line so K2 7→6 is illegal under King-Safety,
no capture and no interposition is possible. Mate is delivered on White’s
4th move, 7 half-moves:

1 N1–3 1…R2–4 2 K1–1 2…R2×N1 3 R1×R2 3…N2–4 4 R1×N2#

The 5 White-move / 9-ply line
1.N1–3 1…R2 5–4 2.R1 2–1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 1×3 3…N2 6–4 4.R1 3–5
4…N2 4–2 5.R1 5–6#
is the often quoted maximal-delay presentation, 9 plies / 5 White moves.
Several colleagues now argue the extra waiting moves R2 4↔5 / N2 4↔6
raise the White king on an open line to R2 once R1 has advanced, i.e.
the K1-safety rule is violated before the final mating move, and the
symmetric K2 7→6 advance used in the 13-ply line is illegal because K2
would be left on the open R1 file. Removing those illegal extensions
collapses the maximal legal defence to the 4 White-move 7-ply line above.

Counting disagreement therefore remains:
* shortest force = 3 White moves = 5 plies
* longest legal force under correct King-Safety = 4 White moves = 7
half-moves, 6 half-moves to the last White move in the 6-ply camp
notation.
* 5 White moves = 9 plies is the widely quoted maximal-stall
presentation, but it relies on King-Safety violations for White after
R1 advances without K1 0→1 being enforced first.

The essential forced content is the N1 1→3 opening and the R1–K2 rook
net; the only check is a rook check and the only mate is R1 <7 with
r+1…6 empty and K2 unable to move to 6. Unresolved is the final
convention for “turns”: per half-move 7 or 9 plies, per first-player
move 4 or 5, per full round 4 or 5.

1. N1 1→3

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

R1 2 is now protected by N1 3 and K1 is still screened from R2 by R1.

The three essentially different Black replies are 1…R2 5×3, 1…N2 6→4 and 1…R2 5→4. 1…R2 5×3 is the textbook minimum

1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2 6→4 3.R1 3×4#

0 K1 . . . 4 R1 . . 7 K2

1…R2 5→4

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

After that White must open the king. The king-safe continuations are

2. K1 0→1  or the equivalent 2.R1 2→1
2…R2 4×3

the capture of the screening knight is forced; 2…R2 4→5 is the same net a move later. 
3. R1 2×3

0 K1 . 3 R1 . 6 N2 7 K2
3…N2 6→4

is the only move that does not put K2 at once on the R1 file; any other N2 move uncovers 6-7 to R1.
4. R1 3×4#

R1 4 –5–6–7 is now a clear rook line. K2 7→6 stays on the R1 line and is illegal under King-Safety, K2 cannot capture R1 and there is no black interposition left; R2 is gone. The position is a legal rook check-mate.

In ply notation the maximal king-safe line is

1.N1 1–3 1…R2 5–4 2.K1 0–1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 2×3 3…N2 6–4 4.R1 3×4#

i.e. White’s fourth move, the seventh half-move of the game. The same content is often written as

1.N1 1–3 1…R2 5–4 2.R1 2–1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 1×3 3…N2 6–4 4.R1 3×4#

The classic minimum is the well known

1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2#

5 plies, three White moves.

R1 1 is now between K1 0 and R2 4.  Black is now forced to remove the
screen.  Up to play the maximally stalling king-safe reply is

2…R2 4×3                         0 K1 1 R1 3 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

3. R1 1×3                         0 K1 . 3 R1 . 6 N2 7 K2

Now K2 is still screened by N2 6 and the only move which does not
immediately expose K2 to R1 3 is

3…N2 6→4                         0 K1 . 3 R1 4 N2 . 7 K2

and the mate is now forced.

4. R1 3×4#                        0 K1 . . . 4 R1 . . 7 K2

R1 4 commands 5–6–7.  K2 7→6 stays on the R1 line and is illegal under
King Safety, K2 cannot capture R1 4 and there is no black interposition
left, R2 is gone.  The position is a legal rook check-mate.

In half-move notation

1 N1 1–3   1…R2 5–4
2 R1 2–1   2…R2 4×3
3 R1 1×3   3…N2 6–4
4 R1 3×4#

i.e. White’s 4th move, the 7th half-move of the game.  In ordinary
mate-in-n notation this is mate in four for the mating side, 7 plies
in total, 4 moves of Player 1 and 3 moves of Player 2.  Counting a
turn as a single move that is the 7th turn of the game, 4 turns of the
first player.  The 5-ply 1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2#
line is the 3-move, 5-ply minimum forced win.  The 9-ply 5-White-move
shuttle 1…R2 5–4 2.R1 2–1 2…R2 4→5 3.N1 3×5 3…N2 6–4 4.R1 1×4
4…K2 7–6 5.N1 5–7# which is often quoted is not King-Safety legal in
the form in which it is usually written; once the King-Safety rule
K1 must not be left on an open line to R2 is enforced the waiting
K2 7→6 / N1 shuttle disappears and the strictly legal maximal-stall
realisation collapses to the 7-ply/4-White-move line above. ∎

6.text:
Under rook only checking the only useful first move is the shield

1. N1 1-3         0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened from R2 by R1 and R1 is now protected by N1 3.
Up to symmetry the only tenacious second player replies are
1…R2 5×3, 1…N2 6-4 and the stalling

1…R2 5-4      0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

The king has to be opened.  Up to the 2.R1 2-1 = 2.K1 0-1
equivalence the only king-safe continuation is

2. K1 0-1       2…R2 4×3
0 .1 K1 2 R1 3 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

the screen has to be taken, 2…R2 4-5 is the same net a move later.
3. R1 2×3       0 .1 K1 3 R1 . 6 N2 7 K2

3…N2 6-4 is the only move which does not put K2 at once on the R1
file, any other N2 move uncovers 6-7 to R1.  The position is

0 .1 K1 3 R1 4 N2 . 7 K2

and now

4. R1 3×4#

is a legal rook check.  R1 4-5-6-7 is a clear rook line, R2 is gone,
K2 7-6 stays on the R1 line and is illegal under King-Safety,
K2 cannot take on 4 and there is no black interposition left.
In the R1 2-1 notation the same net is

1.N1 1-3 1…R2 5-4
2.R1 2-1 2…R2 4×3
3.R1 1×3 3…N2 6-4
4.R1 3×4#

0 K1 . . . 4 R1 . . 7 K2

i.e. White’s 4th move, the 7th half-move of the game.  In ordinary
mate-in-n notation this is mate in four for White.

The textbook minimum is

1.N1 1-3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2 6-4 3.R1 3×4#

5 plies, White’s 3rd move, the familiar 5-ply/3-move forced mate.  With
optimal Black defence the forced win is therefore 3 White moves minimum,
4 White moves maximum, 5 plies minimum and 7 plies maximum, the 4
White-move / 7-ply line above being the longest king-safe forced win.
In half-move counting this is the 7th move of the game, i.e. the 6th
complete P1/P2 round, the 3-move 5-ply line being the shortest forced
realisation.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m with Colleagues 1 and 12 on the King-Safety collapse. The 7-ply/4-White-move line that keeps getting quoted can’t be made legal once the K1–R2 screen is enforced.

The only first move that does not lose material at once is

1. N1 1→3

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened from R2 by R1 2 and N1 3 now screens R1 from a capture by R2. Up to symmetry the tenacious reply is

1… R2 5→4

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

Now the White king has to come off 0 before any forward rook advance, otherwise R1 vacates the 2-square and K1 0 is on an open line to R2 4. 2.R1 2→1 with K1 still on 0 is illegal under King Safety. The forced tempo is therefore

2. K1 0→1

0 . 1 K1 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened by R1 2 from R2 4. The only king-safe reply is to remove the screen

2… R2 4×3

0 . 1 K1 2 R1 3 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

3. R1 2×3

0 . 1 K1 . 3 R1 . 6 N2 7 K2

Now K2 is still screened by N2 6 and the only move which does not immediately expose K2 to the R1-file is

3… N2 6→4

0 . 1 K1 . 3 R1 4 N2 . 7 K2

and now

4. R1 3×4#

R1 4 attacks K2 7 through 5-6. 5 and 6 are empty, K2 7→6 stays on the R1 line and is illegal under King Safety, K2 cannot take R1 4 and there is no black interposition left. R1 is guarded by the line and N2 has just moved.

That is White’s third effective mating move. In half-move notation it is

1.N1 1–3 1…R2 5–4
2.K1 0–1 2…R2 4×3
3.R1 2×3 3…N2 6–4
4.R1 3×4#

the mate being delivered on White’s 3rd move, the 6th half-move of the game under the normal P1/P2 alternating count. The extra waiting move 4.R1 3–5 4…N2 4–2 5.R1 5–6# that is used to reach the 7-ply/9-ply quotes requires 6…N2 2–4 followed by 7.R1 3–5, but after 6…N2 2–4 the White king on 1 is left with an open line to the enemy rook once R2 is gone and 7.R1 3–5 is not King-Safe for White. Removing that illegal extension collapses the maximal defence to the 6-ply/3-White-move line above, i.e. a forced win in six turns with optimal defence. The familiar 5-ply mate

1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2#

is the minimum, and the line above is the longest King-Safety-compliant defence.

4.text:
On the 0-7 file the only check that can be given is a rook check and the
only way to stop a rook check on the right hand side is to keep a man
on the 3-6 interval between R1 and K2.  The first move which does not
lose the R1 at once and which keeps K1 covered by R1 is unique up to
symmetry

1. N1 1-3            0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened from R2 by R1 2 and N1 3 now screens R1 from a
capture by R2.  Up to symmetry the three essentially different
second player replies are 1…R2×N1, 1…N2 6-4 and 1…R2 5-4.  The
first two are met at once by

1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2-4 3.R1×N2#

5 plies, White’s 3rd move, the textbook mate in three.  The longest
king safe defence is the rook retreat

1…R2 5-4     0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

After that the only tempo preserving continuation which keeps K1
safe from R2 is

2. K1 0-1

K1 1 is still screened from R2 4 by R1 2.  The maximally stalling
king safe reply is

2…R2 4-5         . K1 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

Now

3. N1 3×5         . K1 2 R1 . . 5 N1 6 N2 7 K2

removes the Black rook and K1 stays safe.  Black has to keep the
king out of the R1 line

3…N2 6-4         . K1 2 R1 . . 5 N1 4 N2 7 K2

and now

4. R1 2×4         . K1 . 4 R1 . 5 N1 4 N2 7 K2

keeps K1 screened and opens the R1–K2 battery.  The only king safe
move is

4…K2 7-6         . K1 . 4 R1 . 5 N1 4 N2 6 K2

K2 6 is still screened from R1 4 by N1 5.  The mate is now forced

5. N1 5-3#

R1 4-5-6-7 is a clear rook line.  5 is vacated by the knight, R1 4
checks K2 6, 6-5 is on the rook line and 6-7 is on the rook line, R2
is gone and N2 is gone so there is no interposition and no capture.
K2 has no legal king safe move.  In half move notation

1 N1 1-3   1…R2 5-4
2 K1 0-1   2…R2 4-5
3 N1 3×5   3…N2 6-4
4 R1 2×4   4…K2 7-6
5 N1 5-3#

nine half moves in all, White’s fifth move, the familiar 5-move,
9-ply forced mate.  In White move counting this is mate in five, the
usual minimum being the 5-ply

1.N1-3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2-4 3.R1×N2#

mate in three, i.e. three White moves, five plies.  With the
conventional “a turn = a half move’’ counting this is the 9-turn
maximally stalled forced win, the 4 White-move 7-ply line

1.N1-3 1…R2 5-4 2.K1 0-1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 2×3 3…N2 6-4 4.R1 3×4#

being the 7-ply / 4 White-move essentially unique maximal-delay core.
∎

10.text:
On the 0-7 file the only check is a rook check and the only way to keep
K1 off the R2 line is to keep a man on the 1-4 interval.  The only
developing first move which does not lose material at once and which
keeps K1 covered is

1. N1 1-3     0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

up to symmetry the three tenacious replies are 1…R2×N1, 1…N2 6-4 and
the rook retreat 1…R2 5-4.  1…R2×N1 is the text book minimum

1.N1-3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2-4 3.R1×N2#                5 plies

The longest king safe defence is

1…R2 5-4        0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

The rook must stay in front of K1.  The maximal stalling White
continuation is the rook shuffle

2. R1 2-1       0 K1 1 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

2…R2 4-5 is the longest king safe reply.  2…R2 4×3 is the 7-ply
realisation

2…R2 4×3 3.R1 1×3 3…N2 6-4 4.R1 3×4#

With the 4-5 defence

3. N1 3×5       0 K1 1 R1 . . 5 N1 6 N2 7 K2

removes the only piece which can keep K1 in check, K1 is still safe
because R1 1 still blocks R2.

3…N2 6-4 is forced, K2 is still screened by N1 5.

4. R1 1×4       0 K1 . . . 4 R1 5 N1 4 N2 7 K2

R2 is gone so K1 is automatically safe.  The only king safe Black move
now is

4…K2 7-6

K2 6 is interposed by N1 5 between R1 4 and K2 6.

5. N1 5-7#

R1 4-5-6-7 is now open.  K2 6-5, K2 6-7 and K2 6×R1 4 are all on the
R1 line and are illegal under the King-Safety rule and there is no
capture of R1 and no interposition left.  The position is a legal rook
check-mate.

In half-move notation

1 N1 1-3     1…R2 5-4
2 R1 2-1     2…R2 4-5
3 N1 3×5     3…N2 6-4
4 R1 1×4     4…K2 7-6
5 N1 5-7# 

9 half-moves in all, i.e. five moves of the mating side.  The
text-book minimum is the 5-ply 1.N1-3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2-4
3.R1×N2# mate in three White moves.  In White-move counting this is the
familiar mate in five, 9 plies, 5th White move, the 5th round with the
mate delivered on the 9th individual move of the game.  If a “turn’’ is
counted as a White move the forced win is mate in five, 9 plies in the
usual alternating-move count.

3.text:
On the 0–7 file the only check that can be given is a rook check and
the only way of stopping a rook check on the right hand side is to keep
a man on the 3–6 interval between R1 and K2.  The first move which does
not lose material at once and which keeps K1 screened from R2 is

1. N1 1–3    0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

and the only tenacious replies are 1…R2 5×3 and 1…R2 5–4.  1…R2 5×3
is the textbook

1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2# ,

5 plies, White’s 3rd move.  The longest king-safe defence is the rook
retreat

1…R2 5–4     0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 6 N2 7 K2 .

Up to symmetry the only tempo keeping White continuations are
2.K1 0–1 and 2.R1 2–1.  With the maximal stalling defence

2. R1 2–1    0 K1 1 R1 3 N1 4 R2 6 N2 7 K2
2…R2 4×3    0 K1 1 R1 3 R2 6 N2 7 K2
3. R1 1×3    0 K1 . 3 R1 6 N2 7 K2
3…N2 6–4    0 K1 . 3 R1 4 N2 7 K2

the game is now

K1 0 , R1 3 , N2 4 , K2 7

and

4. R1 3×4#

is a legal rook check.  R1 4–5–6–7 is open, K2 7–6 stays on the R1
line and is illegal under the King-Safety rule, K2 cannot take R1 4
and there is no black interposition left.  The position is a legal
rook check-mate.

In half-move notation

1 N1 1–3      1…R2 5–4
2 R1 2–1      2…R2 4×3
3 R1 1×3      3…N2 6–4
4 R1 3×4#

i.e. the mate is delivered on White’s 4th move, the 7th ply of the
game.  In the usual “mate in n’’ counting this is mate in four for the
mating side, the 5-ply mate

1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2#

being the minimal forced line.  The 9-ply 4.R1 3–5 4…N2 4–2
5.R1 5–6# etc. lines that are quoted in the room are not king-safe:

2.text:
On the 0-7 file the only check that can be given is a rook check and a
rook check on the right hand side is inescapable iff

R1 = r < 7, r+1 … 6 empty

so that the only flight square 7→6 is still on the rook line.
With

0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is screened from R2 by R1 and K2 is screened from R1 by R2–N2.
R1 2×5 is an immediate stalemate.  The only first move which keeps the
K1–R2 screen intact and which opens the K1 advance is

1. N1 1–3

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

Up to symmetry the defence which keeps the line to K2 closed the
longest is

1… R2 5–4

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

The king can only be kept safe by keeping a man on the 1–4 line.  The
tempo preserving first move is

2. K1 0–1

0 . 1 K1 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

The only king-safe replies of Black are the capture of the screen and the
rook retreat.  The tenacious continuation is

2… R2 4×3
0 . 1 K1 2 R1 3 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

3. R1 2×3
0 . 1 K1 . 3 R1 . 6 N2 7 K2

The only move which keeps K2 out of the R1 file is

3… N2 6–4
0 . 1 K1 . 3 R1 4 N2 . 7 K2

and now

4. R1 3×4#

R1 4 attacks K2 7 through the empty squares 5,6.  K2 7→6 stays on
the R1 line and is illegal under the King-Safety rule, K2 cannot take
R1 4 and there is no black interposition left.  In ordinary chess
notation this is

1 N1–3 1…R2–4 2 K1–1 2…R2×N1 3 R1×R2 3…N2–4 4 R1×N2#

the mate being delivered on White’s 4th move, i.e. on the 7th half-move
of the game, the 4th full round.  The classic minimum is the well known

1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2#

5 plies, three White moves, mate in three.  The textbook 9-ply
5-White-move maximal-stall presentation

1.N1–3 1…R2 5–4 2.R1 2–1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 1×3 3…N2 6–4
4.R1 3–5 4…N2 4–2 5.R1 5–6#

is the 9 half-move, five White move, line which is usually quoted.
Once the King-Safety requirement that a moving king must not be left on
the open rook line is enforced the two waiting moves R2 4↔5/N2 4↔6 are
illegal and the maximal legal defence collapses to the 4 White move,
7 half-move mate above.  This is the 3-move, 5-ply minimum and the
4-move, 7-ply maximal legal forced win of the position. ∎

8.text:
On the 0-7 file a check can only be given by a rook and a rook check on
K2 can only be met by a king move, a capture of the rook or an
interposition on the unique square between rook and king.

The first move which keeps K1 covered by R1 and does not at once
stalemate is

1. N1 1-3               0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened from R2 by R1 2. Up to symmetry the only
tenacious second player replies are

1...R2 5×3 , 1...N2 6-4 , 1...R2 5-4

1...R2×N1 is the textbook minimum

1.N1-3 1...R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2...N2-4 3.R1×N2#

5 plies, three White moves, the rook on 4 commanding 5-6-7.

The longest legal defence is the rook retreat

1...R2 5-4   0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

The only king-safe tempo is

2. K1 0-1   . K1 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

Now the only stalling reply is the rook shuttle

2...R2 4-5   . K1 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

and the forced net is

3. N1 3×5      . K1 2 R1 . . 5 N1 6 N2 7 K2
3...N2 6-4    . K1 2 R1 . 4 N2 5 N1 . 7 K2
4. R1 2×4     . K1 . . 4 R1 5 N1 . 7 K2

R1 4 is still screened from K1 by the empty 1-2-3 interval and the
R1-K2 file is now closed only by N1 5.  The only king-safe defence is

4...K2 7-6    . K1 . . 4 R1 5 N1 . 6 K2

and the rook line is opened by the waiting knight move

5. N1 5-3 #

R1 4-5-6 is now clear, K2 6-5/7 stays on the R1 line and is illegal
under King Safety, K2 cannot capture R1 and there is no black
interposition left.  In half move notation

1 N1 1-3   1...R2 5-4   2 K1 0-1   2...R2 4-5   3 N1 3×5
3...N2 6-4   4 R1 2×4   4...K2 7-6   5 N1 5-3 #

nine plies in all, four complete P1+P2 pairs and the delivering
move, i.e. mate on White’s fifth move.  The same net is obtained with
the symmetric 2.R1 2-1 defence

1.N1-3 1...R2 5-4 2.R1 2-1 2...R2 4-5 3.N1×5 3...N2-4
4.R1×4 4...K2-6 5.N1-3#

so that with best defence White needs five of his own moves, nine
half-moves in total.  The familiar 7-ply maximal-stall realisation

1.N1-3 1...R2 5-4 2.K1 0-1 2...R2×N1 3.R1×R2 3...N2-4
4.R1×N2#

is the 4 White-move, 7-ply version of the same net, and the
text-book minimum is the 3 White-move, 5-ply

1.N1-3 1...R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2...N2-4 3.R1×N2#

mate in three. ∎

public_text.1:
The king-safety rule is the audit that collapses the longer lines. The only first move that keeps K1 covered from R2 and does not lose material at once is

1. N1 1-3
0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened by R1 2 and N1 3 now screens R1 from an immediate R2 capture. Up to symmetry the tenacious replies are 1…R2 5-4 and 1…N2 6-4. The 1…N2 6-4 / K2 7-6 idea used for the 13-ply line is illegal: after

2.K1 0-1 2…K2 7-6

The maximally stalling legal defence is the rook shuffle.

1.N1 1-3 1…R2 5-4
0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

White has to open the king before any forward rook advance, otherwise K1 would be left on the R2 line.

2.K1 0-1
0 . 1 K1 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2
K1 is still screened by R1 2 from R2 4.

The only king-safe black reply that does not immediately lose the knight is

2…R2 4×3
0 . 1 K1 2 R1 3 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

Any retreat of R2 to 5 re-opens  R1 2-4 and the mate comes a move earlier.

3.R1 2×3
0 . 1 K1 . 3 R1 . 6 N2 7 K2
R1 is now between K1 and the enemy rook.

Black must keep K2 out of the R1 file:

3…N2 6-4
0 . 1 K1 . 3 R1 4 N2 . 7 K2

Now

4.R1 3×4 #
0 . 1 K1 . 4 R1 . . . 7 K2

R1 4 attacks K2 7 through 5,6. 5 and 6 are empty, K2 7-6 stays on the rook line and is illegal under King-Safety, K2 cannot capture R1 4 because the rook is protected by the line, and there is no black man that can interpose between 4 and 7 in one move. R2 is gone.

That is a legal rook checkmate. It is White’s 3rd effective mating move in the symmetric exposition and White’s 4th move in the R2 5-4 notation, i.e.

1 N1 1-3   1…R2 5-4
2 K1 0-1   2…R2 4×3
3 R1 2×3   3…N2 6-4
4 R1 3×4 #

seven half-moves in total. Counting a turn as a single player move in the convention the group has been using for the maximal stall, the mate is delivered on the 6th turn of the game, three White moves, six plies from the start. The extra waiting move 7.R1 3-5 that is quoted in the 7-move / 13-ply line is not king-safe for White after 6…N2 2-4, and the K2 7-6 waiting move is illegal under King-Safety. Once those illegal extensions are removed the longest king-safe forced win collapses to the 6-turn, White-3, six-ply line above, which is the conventional maximal-delay mate of the position.
public_text.7:
I think the King-Safety refutation that Colleague 7 points out is the decisive one and it collapses the 7-ply / 13-ply maximal lines that keep getting quoted.

The only first move that does not lose material at once and keeps K1 screened from R2 is

1. N1 1→3          0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

and up to symmetry the only tenacious replies are 1…R2 5→4 and the symmetric 1…N2 6→4. The symmetric waiting line is the one that is used to get to the 13-ply story:

1.N1 1-3 1…N2 6-4
2.K1 0-1 2…K2 7-6

is illegal. After 2.K1 0-1 the White king is still screened by R1 2, but K2 on 6 is now on the same open file as R1 2-6 with 3,4,5 empty. The King-Safety rule requires the moving player’s king not to be under attack by an opponent’s rook after the move. 2…K2 7→6 leaves K2 in the rook line of R1, so the symmetric king advance that the long line relies on is not available. The same problem kills the 2…R2 4→3 capture that is sometimes written as 2…R2 4×3 after 2.K1 0-1, because the knight on 3 is gone and the White king would be left on the open R2 line.

Once that illegality is enforced the longest king-safe defence is the rook stall.

1.N1 1-3 1…R2 5-4
0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

K1 has to come off 0 before R1 can be used forward, otherwise K1 is left on the open R2 line. 2.K1 0-1 is therefore forced and still keeps K1 screened by R1 2.

2…R2 4×3 is then the only king-safe way to remove the screen. 
0 K1 . 2 R1 3 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

3.R1 2×3
0 K1 . 3 R1 . 6 N2 7 K2

Now K2 is still screened by N2 6 and the only move which does not immediately expose K2 to R1 3 is

3…N2 6→4
0 K1 . 3 R1 4 N2 . 7 K2

and the rook check is forced

reflection_text.4:
The position is symmetric on a 0-7 file. Only a rook can give check and King-Safety forbids a king to be left on/ move onto an open rook line of the opponent.

The only first move that keeps K1 screened from R2 and does not lose the rook at once is

1. N1 1→3   0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened by R1 2 and R1 is now protected by N1 3. Up to symmetry the tenacious replies are 1…R2×N1, 1…N2 6→4 and the stalling 1…R2 5→4.

Minimum forced line
1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2#
5 half-moves, 3 White moves. R1 on 4 commands 5-6-7, no interposition, K2 7→6 stays on the rook line.

Maximal stalling defence
1…R2 5→4   0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

K1 has to be opened before any forward rook advance, otherwise K1 would be left on an open R2 line. The two king-safe tempos are 2.K1 0→1 and the equivalent 2.R1 2→1. In both cases the longest king-safe Black reply is the rook shuffle 2…R2 4→5.

The maximally stalling legal net is
1.N1 1-3 1…R2 5-4
2.K1 0-1 2…R2 4-5
3.N1 3×5 3…N2 6-4
4.R1 2×4 4…K2 7-6
5.N1 5-3#

or with the 2.R1 2-1 notation
1.N1 1-3 1…R2 5-4
2.R1 2-1 2…R2 4-5
3.N1 3×5 3…N2 6-4
4.R1 1×4 4…K2 7-6
5.N1 5-7#

After 4… the N1 on 5 still interposes between R1 4 and K2, so K2 7→6 is King-Safe for Black and K1 is still screened from the now gone R2. Moving the knight away on move 5 opens R1 4-5-6-7. K2 is now in a rook check, 6-5 and 6-7 stay on the rook line and are illegal under King-Safety, no capture and no interposition is possible.

That is 9 half-moves, 5 White moves, the classic 9-ply maximal stall. The 7-ply / 4 White-move core
1.N1–3 1…R2–4 2.K1–1 2…R2×N1 3.R1×R2 3…N2–4 4.R1×N2#
is the 7 half-move shortcut obtained by 2…R2 4×3 instead of 2…R2 4-5.

The 13-ply symmetric K2 7→6 waiting lines quoted in round 0 are illegal once King-Safety is enforced: a bare K2 7→6 with an open R1 file leaves K2 under attack by R1 2. The illegal waiting extensions collapse to the legal core above.

Counting convention remains disputed. Minimum forced win is 5 plies / 3 White moves. Longest King-Safety-compliant forced win is 9 plies / 5 White moves, often reported as the 9-turn forced win. The 7-ply / 4 White-move line is the most often quoted maximal-delay core after the illegal K2 advances are removed.
reflection_text.8:
The rook-only check and the King-Safety audit are the whole game. The only first move that keeps K1 screened from R2 and does not lose material at once is 1.N1 1→3. 0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2. 

Minimum forced content is

1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2#
5 plies, three White moves, R1 on 4 commands 5-6-7 and K2 has no flight.

The tenacious defence is the rook retreat 1…R2 5→4. K1 has to be opened before White can use R1 forward. Two king-safe continuations are in circulation:

* 2.K1 0→1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 2×3 3…N2 6→4 4.R1 3×4#. 
7 plies, four White moves. R1 4 attacks K2 7 through 5-6, K2 7→6 is still on the rook line and illegal, no interposition, R2 gone. This is the 7-ply/4-White move core that is quoted as the longest king-safe line once the illegal K2 7→6 waiting advances with an unblocked R1 file are removed.

* 2.R1 2→1 2…R2 4→5 3.N1 3×5 3…N2 6→4 4.R1 1×4 4…K2 7→6 5.N1 5→3#. 
9 plies, five White moves. After 3.N1×R2 the Black rook is gone, K1 stays screened by R1 1, the 4…K2 7→6 is king-safe because N1 on 5 blocks R1 4–6, and 5.N1 5→3 opens R1 4–5–6–7. K2 6→5/7 and K2×R1 are all on the rook line and illegal under King-Safety. The symmetric 5.N1 5→7# notation is the same net.

The 13-ply symmetric king-advance lines that use 1…N2 6→4 2.K1 0→1 2…K2 7→6 are illegal once King-Safety is enforced, because with R1 still on 2 the squares 3-4-5 are empty and K2 on 6 would sit on the open R1 file. That collapses the long 13-ply story.

Disagreement remains on turn counting and on whether R1 can be advanced before K1 moves. The maximally stalling king-safe defence that survives the King-Safety audit is the 7-ply/4-White move line above; with the R1 2→1 tempo the 9-ply/5-White move shuttle is also king-safe and is the 9 half-move, five first-player move maximal stall quoted in the room. Minimum forced win is the 5-ply/3-White move mate. Turn = half-move gives 9, i.e. 5 first-player moves, 7 plies/4 first-player moves in the stricter 2.K1 0→1 interpretation.

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2, K1 is still screened from R2 by R1 2 and N1 3 now screens R1 from an immediate R2 capture.

K1 safety = a man on 1–4 between K1 and R2; K2 safety = a man on 3–6 between K2 and R1.  
K2 7→6 with R1 on 2 and 3-5 empty is illegal; a White rook advance that leaves K1 on an open line to R2 is illegal. Those illegals are what remove the 13-ply symmetric king-shuffle.

1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2#
0 K1 . . . 4 R1 . . 7 K2. R1 4 commands 5-6-7, 6 is still on the rook line and there is no interposition. 5 plies, three White moves. That is the textbook mate in three, the fastest forced realisation.

1…R2 5–4 is the longest king-safe reply.
1.N1–3 1…R2 5–4
0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

The longest king-safe White continuation uses the R1 shuttle, not an early K1 advance.

2.R1 2–1  0 K1 1 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2
R1 1 is between K1 0 and R2 4.  
2…R2 4–5 is the longest king-safe reply; 2…R2 4×3 is the 7-ply realisation.

3.N1 3×5   0 K1 1 R1 . . 5 N1 6 N2 7 K2
R2 is gone, K1 is automatically safe, K2 is still screened by N1 5/N2 6.

3…N2 6–4 is forced.
4.R1 1×4   0 K1 . . 4 R1 5 N1 . 7 K2
R1 4 is screened from K1 and R1–K2 is closed only by N1 5.

4…K2 7–6 is now king-safe: R1 4–5–6 is blocked by N1 5.
5.N1 5–7#
R1 4–5–6–7 is now clear. K2 6–5/7 stays on the R1 line and is illegal under King-Safety, K2 cannot capture R1 and there is no interposition left. R2 is gone and N2 is gone.

1 N1 1–3   1…R2 5–4
2 R1 2–1   2…R2 4–5
3 N1 3×5   3…N2 6–4

1.N1–3 1…R2–4 2.K1–1 2…R2×N1 3.R1×R2 3…N2–4 4.R1×N2#

I am with Colleagues 10, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9 on the rook-shuffle maximal defence. Once the King-Safety rule is applied strictly the screen on the 0-7 file is the whole game, and the screen can be kept for much longer than the six-turn line allows if the rook is shuffled first.

The only developing first move which keeps K1 covered from R2 and does not lose material at once is

1. N1 1-3          0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened by R1 2 and R1 2 is now protected by N1 3. 
Up to symmetry the longest defence is

1…R2 5-4          0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2

The White king does not have to move first. The king-safe tempo is the rook shuffle

2. R1 2-1          0 K1 1 R1 3 N1 4 R2 . 6 N2 7 K2
2…R2 4-5          0 K1 1 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened from R2 by R1 1 and K2 is still screened from R1 1 by N1 3 – R2 5 – N2 6. 

3. N1 3×5          0 K1 1 R1 . . 5 N1 6 N2 7 K2
3…N2 6-4          0 K1 1 R1 . . 5 N1 4 N2 7 K2

The capture removes the only piece which could keep K1 in check and K1 remains safe because R1 1 still blocks R2. K2 is still screened by N1 5.

4. R1 1×4          0 K1 . . . 4 R1 5 N1 . 7 K2
4…K2 7-6          0 K1 . . . 4 R1 5 N1 . 6 K2

Now R2 is gone so K1 is automatically safe. The move 4…K2 7-6 is king-safe for Black because N1 5 now interposes between R1 4 and K2 6. After 1.N1 1-3 the file 1-2-3-4-5-6 is not open for White: R1 4 is screened from K1 by the empty squares 1-3 and N1 5 screens R1 4 from K2 6. That is exactly why the waiting king move is legal here and it is what gives the extra tempo the six-turn audit discards.

The rook line is now forced open

5. N1 5-7#
R1 4-5-6-7 is clear. K2 6-5, K2 6-7 and K2 6×R1 4 are all on the R1 line and are illegal under the King-Safety rule, there is no capture of R1 and no black man left to interpose between 4 and 7. R2 is gone and N2 is gone.

In alternating half-move notation

1 N1 1-3     1…R2 5-4
2 R1 2-1     2…R2 4-5
3 N1 3×5     3…N2 6-4
4 R1 1×4     4…K2 7-6
5 N1 5-7#

That is 9 half-moves in all, five moves of the mating side. With the symmetric 2.K1 0-1 notation the same net is

1.N1–3 1…R2–4 2.K1–1 2…R2–5 3.N1×R2 3…N2–4 4.R1×N2 4…K2–6 5.N1–3#

The textbook minimum remains

1.N1–3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2–4 3.R1×N2#

5 plies, three White moves, mate in three. The longest King-Safety compliant forced win is therefore mate in five for Player 1, nine individual moves of the game, the 7-ply four White-move core 1.N1–3 1…R2 5-4 2.K1 0-1 2…R2 4×3 3.R1 2×3 3…N2 6-4 4.R1 3×4# being the same net with the 2…R2 4×3 shortcut.
